variants.title: EJ255 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: While "EJ255" is used as a single engine code, there are several distinct revisions across the production run. The differences matter - particularly when buying a replacement, as not all EJ255 variants are direct swaps. ### EJ255 Version 1 - 2003-2005 (SG Forester XT, early Legacy GT) - Fitted to: Subaru SG Forester XT (2003-2005) , Subaru BL/BP Legacy GT (2003-2005) - Key technical difference: Uses the AB440 shortblock - the same shortblock as the 2004-2006 STI EJ257 . Single AVCS, TD04 turbocharger. Power: 155kW (208 hp) at 5600rpm, 320Nm at 3600rpm . - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family head gasket and turbo failure patterns above. Early versions are more prone to oil starvation issues. - Interchange note: Direct swap with later EJ255 variants requires ECU reflash and may need different turbo plumbing. ### EJ255 Version 2 - 2005-2008 (GD/GG Impreza WRX, SG Forester XT) - Fitted to: Subaru GD/GG Impreza WRX (2005-2007) , Subaru SG Forester XT (2005-2008) - Key technical difference: Revised compression ratio (9.0:1 vs 8.2:1), power increased to 169kW (227 hp) at 5600rpm . Single AVCS, TD04 turbo. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family patterns. - Interchange note: Direct swap with Version 1 requires ECU update; physical mounting is identical. ### EJ255 Version 3 - 2008-2014 (GE/GH Impreza WRX, SH Forester XT) - Fitted to: Subaru GE/GH Impreza WRX (2007-2014) , Subaru SH Forester XT (2008-2012) - Key technical difference: Revised cylinder heads (D25 heads) , revised ECU calibration. Power: 169kW (227 hp) at 5200rpm, 320Nm at 2800rpm for standard WRX ; 195kW (262 hp) at 6000rpm, 343Nm at 4000rpm for later WRX (2008-2014) . VF52 turbo on later WRX models (instead of TD04). - Sub-code-specific failure note: The VF52 turbo is more durable than the TD04 but still suffers oil starvation if maintenance is poor. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with earlier EJ255 versions - ECU, turbo, and wiring loom differ significantly. ### EJ255 S-Edition - 2011-2012 (SH Forester S-Edition) - Fitted to: Subaru SH Forester S-Edition (2011-2012) - Key technical difference: Higher state of tune - 193kW (259 hp) at 6000rpm, 347Nm at 2800-4800rpm . 5-speed automatic only. Dual AVCS. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Higher boost places additional stress on head gaskets and turbo. Shares the family failure patterns but at slightly elevated risk. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with manual-transmission EJ255s - ECU, loom, and transmission compatibility differ.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EJ255 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used EJ255 makes sense only if it comes with documented evidence of head gasket replacement (MLS units) and a recent timing belt service. Without this documentation, a used EJ255 is a high-risk purchase - head gasket failure can appear within months of installation, and a broken timing belt writes off the engine. Given the EJ255 is an interference engine, any used unit without belt history is a gamble.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper EJ255 recon addresses the known weak points: new MLS head gaskets (not factory-spec), new timing belt kit with tensioner and idlers, new water pump, new turbocharger oil feed lines, and a thorough inspection of the turbocharger itself. Reconditioned units typically include a 12-month warranty and are the sweet spot for most UK owners - you get the reliability upgrades without the cost of a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full EJ255 rebuild is justified when you want to keep a specific vehicle (e.g. a clean Impreza WRX or Forester XT with low body mileage) and want the engine to last another 100,000+ miles. An upgraded rebuild should include forged pistons (the factory cast pistons are a weak point on higher-mileage units), ARP head studs, a fully reconditioned turbocharger, and a new oil pump. Budget £3,500-£5,500 for a quality rebuild.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All of our vetted UK Subaru specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit - nationwide delivery and recovery available, with warranties that cover both parts and labour.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The EJ255 sits in performance Subarus with strong enthusiast following - Impreza WRX values range from £3,000-£12,000 depending on condition and mileage; Forester XT values £3,000-£9,000; Legacy GT £2,500-£8,000. A reconditioned EJ255 at £2,200-£4,000 represents 25-60% of vehicle value - generally viable for most examples. However, for a high-mileage (£3,000-£4,000) Impreza WRX or Forester XT, a full rebuild at £5,500 may approach or exceed the vehicle's value. In those cases, evaluate the car's overall condition, rust, and interior before committing. A clean, low-mileage example justifies the spend; a tired one may be better broken for parts .

items.answer: A reconditioned EJ255 supply-only costs £2,200-£4,000, with fitted prices from £3,200-£5,200. Used units start from £1,800 supply-only. Rebuilt engines with upgraded internals cost £3,500-£5,500 supply-only.

items.question: What are the most common EJ255 engine problems?
items.answer: The EJ255 suffers from head gasket failure (typically 80k-120k miles), turbocharger wear (90k-150k miles), and timing belt failure if the 105k-mile/105-month service is missed. Head gasket replacement with MLS upgrades costs £1,200-£2,500. Turbo rebuild £400-£800; new turbo £600-£1,500. Preventative timing belt service £500-£900.
bullets: Head gasket replacement with MLS upgrades costs £1,200-£2,500.

items.question: Which Subaru models use the EJ255 engine?
items.answer: The EJ255 was fitted to the Subaru Impreza WRX (2005-2014), Forester XT (2003-2013), Legacy GT (2003-2014), Outback XT (2003-2009), and Tribeca (2005-2014). Check your model’s compatibility
bullets: The Impreza WRX is the highest‑volume application.
Forester XT and Legacy GT are also common in the UK.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned EJ255?
items.answer: A reconditioned EJ255 is the safer choice - it includes new MLS head gaskets, a full timing kit, and a 12-month warranty. Used units are only recommended if they come with documented head gasket and timing belt history. A used EJ255 without history is a high-risk purchase.
bullets: Used units are only recommended if they come with documented head gasket and timing belt history.
A used EJ255 without history is a high‑risk purchase.

items.question: What’s the difference between EJ255 and EJ257?
items.answer: The EJ257 is the STI‑spec version with stronger internals (forged pistons, better rods), a larger turbo (VF48), and 300 hp versus the EJ255’s 227-265 hp. See the EJ257 page for details
bullets: The EJ255 is more common and cheaper to replace.
The EJ257 is not a direct drop‑in replacement without ECU and wiring changes.

items.question: How long does an EJ255 engine last?
items.answer: With regular servicing (oil changes every 5k-6k miles) and timely timing belt replacements, an EJ255 can exceed 150,000 miles. Head gasket failure often occurs around 80k-120k miles unless upgraded. Turbocharger life depends on oil quality and driving style.
